recipe.title: Dump-and-Go Crockpot Salsa Verde Chicken Bowls
recipe.summary: Creamy salsa verde chicken with black beans and corn served over cauliflower rice with avocado, cilantro, and lime for approximately 42 grams of protein and 375 calories.
recipe.story: Chicken goes into the crockpot first, followed by Daisy cottage cheese and Herdez salsa verde. At night, shred and stir the creamy chicken mixture, microwave the cauliflower rice, and add fresh toppings.
recipe.serving_size: 10 ounces chicken mixture with 3/4 cup cauliflower rice, 1/8 avocado, cilantro, and a lime wedge
ingredients: 2 pounds raw boneless skinless chicken breast
1 (15-ounce) can black beans, drained and rinsed
2 (10-ounce) bags Birds Eye Steamfresh Original Riced Cauliflower
3/4 medium avocado, divided into six equal portions
instructions: In the morning, place the chicken breasts in the bottom of a 6-quart crockpot.
Spread the Daisy cottage cheese over the chicken, then pour the Herdez salsa verde over the cottage cheese.
Add the drained black beans and corn. Sprinkle the Knorr bouillon, cumin, granulated garlic, and onion powder over everything.
Cover and cook on LOW for 7 to 8 hours, until the chicken reaches 165°F and shreds easily.
At night, shred the chicken directly in the crockpot and stir the shredded chicken and contents of the crockpot together until the sauce looks creamy.
Cook the Birds Eye cauliflower rice according to the package directions.
For each serving, place 3/4 cup cauliflower rice in a bowl and top with 10 ounces of the creamy chicken mixture.
Garnish each bowl with 1/8 avocado, 1 tablespoon cilantro, and 1 lime wedge.
tips: Use refrigerated or completely thawed chicken, never frozen chicken, for safe slow-cooker cooking.
The cottage cheese may look separated before stirring; shredding the chicken and stirring thoroughly brings the sauce together.
Measure 10 ounces of crockpot contents per serving.
The two cauliflower-rice bags provide enough for six measured 3/4-cup servings with a small amount left over.
Nutrition is approximate and varies by product label and avocado size.
